body.heading: Where in the world is Switzerland?
paragraphs: Switzerland is a country in Western Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Switzerland is Bern. Bern is called the federal city — Switzerland has no official capital in its rules, but Bern is where the government and parliament sit.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Switzerland speak German, French and Italian. German, French and Italian are joined by Romansh, spoken in some mountain valleys — four national languages in all.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Switzerland is the Swiss franc.

body.heading: How big is Switzerland?
paragraphs: Switzerland covers about 41,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about half the size of Austria.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: The Matterhorn's perfect pyramid towers over car-free Zermatt. Ride the Gornergrat railway for glacier views and spot the peak mirrored in mountain lakes.
Lucerne's covered wooden Chapel Bridge has crossed the Reuss since the 1300s — beyond it, lake steamers and the Pilatus and Rigi mountain railways await.

2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
